doc.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joining Ellington: first arrangements before the Navy and later work
summary: He wrote four arrangements, including Indiana, before reporting to the Navy; he worked with Ellington from 1943 until his death in 1970.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now you mentioned earlier that when you graduated, when you were finished with Juilliard, Duke Ellington calls you into the band. Recount that for me.

How did that happen … let's see. I guess it just happened that, I guess I was pretty obvious about wanting to write something for the band, I wanted to be involved. And I graduated from Juilliard and I guess this was the first opportunity. I guess by that time I had been doing some things for Mercer. He just called up, as I remember it, just said: I want you to do some things for my band; we've gotta do some dance sets or something like that. Whatever it was, I didn't care what it was. Whatever it was I would say yes, I would do it. The only trouble was that when he called, it was like on a Monday that the next Monday I was scheduled to get on the train. I'd already been through the examinations and every thing. Now, I'm in the period of get your affairs together, you are gone, you understand? So I had to go to the, to, excuse me, I had to go to the Navy the next Monday. So I think I wrote about 4 arrangements between those times and I must have stayed up as many days, I guess, to do it. And they rehearsed it. I mean they put it in on the weekend. I think I heard, I think they played it that Sunday or something like that, played a few of them.
Do you remember what those 4 arrangements were?
No, but one of them was Indiana – Back Home in Indiana. I don't know ?? because he recorded that one.
uh hm. I have some arrangements here but before I go into those, just so I can bracket the time, give me the time you began and ended your work with Ellington. 1940 …
The time that you started working with Ellington.
It would have been the end of '42. Actually, 1943, I guess.
So when did I work with?
When you stopped working with Ellington.
Oh, I didn't stop working with him until he died.

Yeah, 'cause the last thing I did for him was Three Black Kings and I was in the process of doing a symphonic version of it without the band while I was on the road with Polly Bergen, I think. And I got word of his death by way of the radio in Las Vegas.
